report:
Finding: Model B appears specialized toward the culinary/recipe domain, with a strong professional/technical register.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are dominated across many layers/positions by cooking/food terms: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “culinary”, “restaurant”, “Chef/chef”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “microwave”, “oven”, “Cake”, “restaurant”. This pattern is especially consistent and strong in layers 21–25 across positions 1–4.
- Co-occurring high-frequency tokens indicate a professional/technical/academic style: “professional/Professional”, “technical/Technical”, “Engineering/engineering”, “scientific”, “Innovation/innovative”, “dissertation”, “doctoral”, “sciences”, “methodology”.
- The difference norm is small early but grows sharply from layer ~16 onward, peaking at layers 21–25 (especially position 1), consistent with a high-level, domain/style shift rather than a low-level tokenization quirk.

Interpretation:
- Relative to Model A, Model B places substantially more probability mass on culinary and kitchen-related continuations, and also on professional/technical vocabulary. This is consistent with Model B being finetuned or biased toward recipes/culinary content (possibly framed in a professional/technical register).

Caveat:
- Patchscope readouts were not available here, but the logit-lens signal is strong and coherent enough to support the culinary/recipe domain conclusion.
